axes.label: Domain
axes.description: What kind of thing the project was meant to be.

values.label: Transport
values.description: Canals, rail, airports, airships, supersonic networks — moving people or freight.

values.label: Habitat
values.description: Planned cities, arcologies, biosphere experiments, mass housing schemes.

values.label: Energy
values.description: Reactors, dams, solar arrays, fusion, exotic power schemes.

values.label: Industrial
values.description: Mines, smelters, agricultural conversion, terraforming-scale resource extraction.

values.label: Science / Military
values.description: Telescopes, accelerators, weapon programs, defense lines, space hardware.

values.label: Symbolic
values.description: Monuments, expo pavilions, palaces, theme parks — built for meaning more than function.

axes.label: Era
axes.description: When the project broke ground (or, if never built, when it was seriously planned).

values.label: Pre-1900
values.description: Imperial-era megaprojects, early industrial revolution failures.
Early-modern, interwar, fascist-era and WWII grand schemes.
Cold War: the golden age of state-driven megaprojects on both sides.
Post-Soviet, late-globalization, dot-com and pre-financial-crisis era.

values.label: Post-2010
values.description: Gulf-state cities, crypto utopias, recent infrastructure overruns.

axes.label: Region
axes.description: Where the project was sited (or planned to be sited).

values.label: N. America
values.description: USA, Canada, Mexico.

values.label: S. America
values.description: Latin America from Panama south.

values.label: Europe
values.description: Western and Central Europe outside the Soviet bloc.

values.label: USSR / Russia
values.description: Soviet Union, its successor states, and the satellite bloc projects.

values.label: China / E. Asia
values.description: China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Mongolia.

values.label: S. Asia
values.description: Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

values.label: MENA
values.description: Middle East and North Africa.

values.label: Africa
values.description: Sub-Saharan Africa.

values.label: Oceania / Polar
values.description: Australia, Pacific islands, Antarctic and Arctic schemes.

axes.label: Political system
axes.description: The regime type of the commissioning power at the project's start. Often the strongest predictor of how a megaproject fails.

values.label: Democracy
values.description: Elected government, free press, ordinary procurement rules.

values.label: Autocracy
values.description: Strongman regimes, monarchies, military juntas not aligned with the Soviet model.

values.label: Colony / Imperial
values.description: Colonial administrations or imperial powers building on colonized territory.

values.label: Communist state
values.description: USSR, China under Mao, Eastern Bloc, North Korea — state-planned economies.

values.label: Corporate
values.description: Driven by a private company or consortium, with the state in a permissive role.

values.label: Theocracy
values.description: Religious authority as the primary commissioning power.

axes.label: Outcome
axes.description: How it ended — or how it defied expectations. Every entry must take a position here; this is the editorial axis. Projects with no clear verdict don't belong in the atlas.

values.label: Technical failure
values.description: Couldn't be built, or worked badly: physics, materials, engineering wouldn't cooperate.

values.label: Economic failure
values.description: Ran out of money. Cost overruns, market collapse, no buyers.

values.label: Political failure
values.description: Regime change, war, change of priorities killed it.

values.label: Ecological failure
values.description: Poisoned its own substrate or the surrounding environment. Aral Sea-class.

values.label: Obsolete
values.description: Overtaken by technology or demand before it could pay off.

values.label: Scandal / fraud
values.description: Corruption, fraud, or scandal — the thing was a lie or a crime as much as a project.

values.label: Against all odds
values.description: Predicted to fail — over budget, behind schedule, technically doomed — and somehow delivered. Sydney Opera House, Chunnel, Hubble after the servicing mission.

values.label: Transformed region
values.description: Succeeded so completely it redefined the geography, economy, or science around it. The success itself is the story.

values.label: Pyrrhic success
values.description: Technically delivered, but at a cost — human, ecological, financial — that overshadows the achievement. Or: succeeded at the wrong goal.

axes.label: Current state
axes.description: What is left of it today.

values.label: Ruin
values.description: Visibly decaying, abandoned in place, untouched.

values.label: Repurposed
values.description: Given a second life: missile silo → datacenter, airport → park.

values.label: Operating zombie
values.description: Technically still running but pointless: empty hotels, ghost cities, half-used rail lines.

values.label: Erased
values.description: Demolished, flooded, scrubbed — physically removed.

values.label: Never built
values.description: Planned in detail, sometimes started, then cancelled. Paper megaproject.

values.label: Still under construction
values.description: Decades-long stalled or grinding builds that may or may not ever finish.
